mantras.title: Jagannathashtakam (verse 1)
mantras.textOriginal:
कदाचित्कालिन्दीतटविपिनसङ्गीतकरवो
मुदा गोपीनारीवदनकमलास्वादमधुपः ।
रमाशम्भुब्रह्मामरपतिगणेशार्चितपदो
जगन्नाथः स्वामी नयनपथगामी भवतु मे ॥
mantras.transliteration:
kadācitkālindītaṭavipinasaṅgītakaravo
mudā gopīnārīvadanakamalāsvādamadhupaḥ |
ramāśambhubrahmāmarapatigaṇeśārcitapado
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapathagāmī bhavatu me ||
mantras.meaning: May Lord Jagannātha become visible to my eyes — he who at times makes music in the groves on the Yamunā's bank, who like a bee joyfully tastes the lotus faces of the cowherd women, and whose feet are worshipped by Lakṣmī, Śiva, Brahmā, Indra and Gaṇeśa.
mantras.editorNotes: Pre-populated 2026-09-28 from a published text; hidden until the temple priest confirms it is recited here. Source notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Source prints variant readings inline: "var कवरो" (for करवो, line 1) and "var भीरी" (line 2) — removed from the text. DISAGREEMENT: vignanam line 2 reads "mudābhīrī nārīvadana…" (मुदाभीरीनारी-, "the Ābhīra (cowherd) women") where the source reads "मुदा गोपीनारी-" — this is exactly the source's own "var भीरी" variant. Same meaning; the source reading was kept. Rest matches.
